Perhaps you have already looked into this, but your posture may be the problem. People can become stuck into bad habits of motion, or even become locked into stressed or "flight" positions. This can affect your overall wellbeing and your mental state. The good part is that correcting your posture does not require difficult exercise, it only requires releasing the tension in your body. Releasing this tension allows your body to move the way it's supposed to.

If you spend significant amounts of time sitting or in your car, there is a good chance your hips have been moved out of place. This will have negative effects all of over your body. I have two suggestions that have helped me (I had severe posture problems, and though I wasn't depressed, my personality and mood have become considerably more positive and open since releasing much of my body's tension).

First, lessons from an Alexander Technique teacher or a Feldenkrais practitioner can be incredibly helpful - both are there to help you get out of bad habits of motion. Bad habits of motion can even interfere with our ability to deal with emotions, as negative emotions can become locked into misused parts of the body. This may sound over the top, but it's quite sensible. By consciously getting rid of bad habits of motion, you will increase your ability to consciously remove other bad habits (like sleeps problems, mental loops).

My other suggestion is to check out these videos (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M1i2a964SbM) from the Franklin Method (similar to the other two methods I mentioned, this one is also about releasing tension, but specifically from the fascia that connect your muscles). The videos will give you practical tips on how to improve your posture. The one I linked is an excellent entry point, but almost all the videos are helpful.

The videos are free. Lessons from Alexander Technique or Feldenkrais cost about 85 dollars.

This route may sound difficult, but I assure you it's incredibly rewarding. These methods will make you more comfortable with and aware of your body, and once you've tasted some improvement, you'll see it's not hard work to fix your posture - it's incredibly liberating and removes stress from your life.

Good luck with your troubles. I personally don't think drugs work for depression, as pharmaceuticals have been shown to be no more helpful than placebo, and less helpful than exercise. I also don't recommend drugs like MDMA, mushrooms, lsd or weed as others have suggested. I'm not saying you shouldn't try them if you really want to, but those drugs really don't have an inherently positive effect on the mind. In fact, you become very suggestible on mushrooms and lsd. If you do try one of those drugs, use them with a close, sober friend with you. Where you are and what you interact with while on the drug can have a huge effect on your experience.

I'm not an exercise guru by any stretch. Yeah the body weight fitness philosophy has worked well for me--someone who's not so hardcore as to spend hours at the gym everyday.

The idea of pitting muscles against themselves is sometimes called dynamic tension. It's distinct from body weight fitness (at least if you're pedantic about the name) but similar in the sense that you can do it anywhere without special equipment.

One simple exercise is to push your hands together in front of your sternum. Keep applying pressure as you extend your hands out and move your arms through their range of motion. It'll look/feel like tai chi but also a bit like a push up.
Ah! Cool. Sorta like holding a plank? But instead of gravity, youre both pushing/pulling with "opposite" muscles, so no eternal force (gravity) is necessary?

Yep. You can also do it with muscles on the opposite side of the same limb but pushing the hands together is easier to describe. Another nice property is that the resistance fades with fatigue so there's less chance of injury.

We did not evolve for an environment that is tightly temperature controlled, uses artificial lighting, and very sterile. Nor did we evolve for food with precise and unchanging nutritional content. Just like we need a sleep cycle and our bodies need blood delivered via a pumping rhythm instead of continuous circulation, there are other cycles and ebb and flow processes and inputs that our bodies expect. Modern life has disrupted these cycles, and in order to operate at full potential, we have to put them back in.

Here are a few things to try that do not involve medical advice:

1) Expose yourself to bright light for at least an hour a day. Get daylight color temperature 30w CFLs instead of regular bulbs, and use them in the morning and afternoon only. Use something dimmer in the evening. At night, use night mode and limit computer screen usage. Find a paper book to read that interests you and read that instead of looking at a screen before you go to bed. Or write / draw with pen and paper.

2) Completely change all of your food sources. Maybe you are not getting enough of something, maybe something is causing an issue. You could also get tested for nutritional deficiency. Sometimes, it is not just about not getting the right stuff, but your body is not absorbing it. If you crave a certain type of food, find out what that craving might be for and satisfy it (unless you are removing that food temporarily to rule out a food allergy).

3) Vitamins are cheap and deficiencies are common. Try them. Others have recommended vitamin D and B12. I do too. When you take B12, take the sublingual (under the tongue) kind. It bypasses a potential absorption problem that some people have.

4) Find something that gives your life purpose and pursue it. The number 1 predictor of a long life is "do you wake up excited about the coming day?" If you cannot think of anything, try running. It tricks your mind into thinking that you have purpose / agency.

5) Interact with people in real life on a regular basis. It could be visiting a good friend every once and a while, or being nice to waitresses at restaurants every other day or more frequently.

6) I am not sure if this will help with depression, but try a really cold shower or dip in a really cold bath for 10 seconds or so. This helps kick off one of the cycles that your body may not be getting from your environment.
